root_cause: the event log's recovery path treated any parse failure at the log's tail as fatal corruption, with no allowance for the three shapes a crash mid-append can leave (unparseable bytes, a record missing its terminal newline, or a syntactically valid record whose batch_id no longer hashes to its own content) even though such a record was never fsynced as a complete unit and so was never acknowledged to any caller

workload_or_seed: CI (Python 3.11), run 34852755086, tests/test_concurrency.py::test_readers_opening_throughout_a_write_run_never_damage_the_store: three read-only opener processes looping open/close while a writer publishes twelve generations
symptom: a read-only opener raised StateError('event log .../eventlog.jsonl is not readable at offset 4076: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 13 ...') from inside Store.__init__'s unconditional clock/frontier scan of the log, landing on the writer's in-flight (not yet fsynced) final record
root_cause: EventLog.batches_from raised StateError on any JSONDecodeError at the tail of the log, correct for a cursor landing mid-record (corruption) but wrong for a torn *final* record a live writer had not finished appending; Store.__init__(read_only=True) skips _recover() by design (recovery is a writer-only act), so trim_torn_tail never ran for a reader, and the unconditional full-log scans in last_tt()/_tt_at_offset() still raised on that in-flight tail. First fix attempt tolerated any torn final record unconditionally and regressed tests/test_eval_corruption.py::test_torn_event_log_tail_is_detected_even_read_only: a corruption sweep appending garbage to a CLOSED store produces bytes indistinguishable, by framing alone, from a live writer not-yet-finished record (both unparseable, no trailing newline, run to end-of-file, starting exactly at the manifest applied offset). Corrected to require two conditions together (Store._compute_reader_torn_tail_floor): the torn record starts at/after the manifest applied event-log offset (tolerate_torn_tail_from, same value trim_torn_tail(applied_offset) uses for a writer) AND some process currently holds writer.lock (Store._writer_lock_is_held, non-blocking flock probe) — a reader never holds this lock itself, so finding it free proves nothing could still be appending. Both hold in the real race; neither holds for the corruption sweep, which stays DETECTED.

workload_or_seed: xzgpu, `tgms replay <eventlog.jsonl> --store <dir> --backend native --compact-every 500` over the 24h longevity soak's log (1,074,952 batches, 314,897,038 bytes)
symptom: the replay process was OOM-killed by the kernel after ~3.4h at ~83 GB anon RSS, having reached manifest generation ~513,024 -- ~160 KB retained per replayed generation -- while store_digest()-relevant content was only ~1.7M entities: retention, not data
root_cause: Postings::by_identity and Postings::by_vid (crates/tgms-engine-core/src/store.rs) are append-only identity indexes with no prune at all, unlike open_rows, which at least prunes per-lookup in read.rs::locate_open. Periodic compaction (compact.rs::compact) physically reseals every row that still exists -- open and closed, since compaction never drops one -- into fresh segments every cycle, and the next lookup (read.rs::index_segments, reached through any correction's close_version -> locate_vid) re-indexes them there, stacking on top of every earlier cycle's now-unreachable entries that nothing ever freed: entries for a superseded cycle's segments become permanently unreachable (their segment id is gone from the current file map, so locate/locate_vid/locate_open silently skip them) but were never removed from the maps themselves. This is the shared engine commit/compaction path (gc() -> evict_segments_not_in), not something specific to the replay reader: reproduced directly with a plain correction + compact()/gc() write loop (no replay involved) showing the same non-plateauing per-commit growth, and confirmed precisely via a new NativeStore::postings_stats() counter (2,190 by_identity/by_vid entries for 400 versions ever committed over 10 compaction cycles, unfixed, against a floor of ~400 fixed).
observed_in_the_wild: Observed 2026-09-15T11:59:50Z on xzgpu during the 24h longevity soak's replay/digest-equivalence check: `tgms replay --compact-every 500` was OOM-killed at ~83 GB anon RSS after ~513,024 generations (~160 KB/generation). Full record: benchmarks/longevity-v1/replay-check-2026-09-15.json (written by a separate lane). The soak's live writer restarted every 30 minutes (~42 lives, `--compact-every-batches 500`) and each life independently showed the same ~160 KB/commit RSS growth rate (median 3,166 kB/s at ~16-24 commits/s) -- the restarts would have masked this same growth on the write path, since the leak is in code the live writer's own periodic compact()+gc() calls just as replay's compact_every does, not in anything specific to replaying an event log.

symptom: two independent top-level Store.ingest_events calls without an explicit disc on the same event both land at intra-call index i, so both get the same default disc (f"#{offset+i}") when offset resets to 0 per call; if the two events also share (src, dst, rel_type), edge_eid() collides and the second event's EdgeVersion is inserted under the first's eid instead of getting its own -- distinct logical edges silently merge into one edge identity
root_cause: tgms/storage/base.py::_ingest_events reads disc = ev.get("disc", f"#{op.get('offset', 0) + i}"); Store.ingest_events (tgms/store.py) supplied that offset from a local `offset = 0` reset at the top of every top-level call, correct only across the INGEST_CHUNK chunks within one call. Caller audit (grep -rn ingest_events scripts/ tgms/ tests/): scripts/build_synth_store.py -- NOT affected, stamps disc explicitly per event by design (the workaround that surfaced this finding). scripts/eval_harness.py::build_dataset, scripts/build_snb_store.py (bulk path), scripts/build_sx_store.py, scripts/build_synth_iv_store.py, tgms/data/loaders.py, tgms/demo.py, and the large majority of tests -- NOT affected, each makes exactly one top-level ingest_events call per store for its whole event list. scripts/build_wiki_talk_store.py -- NOT affected, bypasses Store.ingest_events and manages its own offset local variable correctly across its manual chunk loop (mirrors ingest_events' own accumulation, never resets it). scripts/live_osv_poller.py / tgms/data/osv_loader.py -- NOT affected, does not call ingest_events at all (writes assert_node/assert_edge/retract/correct directly). scripts/longevity_run.py::apply_correction_via_public_api's a1_events branch -- AFFECTED: calls store.ingest_events(op['events'], ...) once per correction with exactly one event, no explicit disc, so every such call landed at i=0 (disc '#0') under the bug; do_correction() applies this at random throughout every longevity_run.py execution whose --mix includes correction weight (the default 'balanced' mix: correction=10). scripts/eval_writes.py::bench_append -- AFFECTED in principle: repeated top-level ingest_events calls at batch sizes 1/10/100/1000 without explicit disc on one store instance; low practical impact since it is a disposable-temp-store throughput benchmark, not a persisted record. scripts/eval_concurrency.py's writer loop -- repeated top-level ingest_events calls, but src/dst labels are constructed from a monotonically-increasing counter never reused, so no two events can ever share (src, dst, rel_type) regardless of disc; not practically affected.
